summary: Eshin Nishimura was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Hanazono and Kyoto universities, and under Zenkei Shibayama, he taught at Carleton College and served as president, vice president, and director at Hanazono University and director of the Institute for Zen Studies.
Esho Kawasaki worked in Buddhist studies. He served as director of the Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 1999) and president of Kyushu Ryukoku Gakkai (attested 2002).

Esho Mikogami worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He was a professor at Ryukoku University from circa 1974 to 2003, served as president of the Ryukoku Buddhist Society in 1997, and founded Indogaku Chibettogaku Kenkyū.

Esho Sasaki was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held posts as an assistant professor at Ikenobo Junior College (attested 1979) and as a professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1991).
Esho Yamaguchi worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and held posts at Ritsumeikan University and Osaka University, where he served as professor from circa 1968 to 1982.

Ester Bianchi specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from Ca' Foscari University and EPHE under Jean-Noël Robert and Alfredo Cadonna, later holding positions at Ca' Foscari, the University of Florence, and the University of Perugia.
Ethan Kroll is an Indologist who worked at Baker McKenzie and was an editorial board member for Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies, both attested in 2012.
Etienne Vermeersch was a philosopher who studied at Ghent University from circa 1953 to 1958. He later held an academic appointment at Ghent University from 1967 to 1997.

Etsuaki Teraishi worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as an assistant professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and as a special researcher with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2001).

Eugen Hultzsch was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and archaeology. Educated at Leipzig and Vienna under Georg Bühler, he served as Government Epigraphist in India and later as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Halle (1903–1925).

Eugen Pander was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Polytechnikum Riga (~1872–1876) and served as a professor of economics and lecturer in Russian and German at Tongwen Guan in 1881.
Eugen Prym was a linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Bonn from circa 1861 to 1865 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1869 to 1913.

Eugen Wilhelm worked in Iranian, Central Asian, Indological, and linguistic studies. He studied under August Schleicher (~1864–1868) and served as a professor at the University of Jena from circa 1869 to 1923.

Eugene Watson Burlingame was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Charles Rockwell Lanman. He held positions at the University of Pennsylvania, Johns Hopkins University, and served as Lecturer on Pāli at Yale University (~1920–1932).

Eugene Y. Wang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and art history. He studied under Wu Hung and John M. Rosenfield, and held posts at the University of Chicago and Harvard University, becoming Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Professor of Asian Art.
Eugeni d'Ors was a philosopher who studied at the University of Barcelona (~1897–1903) and Universidad Central (~1904–1905). He later held an academic post at Universidad Central circa 1927.

Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv (~1919–1924). He held posts at the University of Lviv, Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń, and served as head of Indology at the University of Warsaw.

Eugène Burnouf was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He served as secretary of the Société Asiatique and taught at the Collège de France (1832–1852).
Eugène Jacquet was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He pursued his studies under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat from circa 1828 to 1832 and under Eugène Burnouf from circa 1832 to 1838.

Eugène Obermiller was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky (~1921–1925) and Dondub Buddhayin (1929), and served as Section Secretary at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1930–1935).
